question.problem:
The manufacturing times of bicycle frames are normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ minutes and a standard deviation of $5$ minutes. Additionally, $25%$ of frames are completed in under $48$ minutes. Find the percentage of frames that take longer than $52$ minutes. **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5517\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ | $\,0.5596\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5910\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ | $\,0.5987\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6293\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ | $\,0.6368\,$ |

Approximately
{{field-1}}$%$ of the frames take longer than $52$ minutes.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the time required to manufacture a bicycle frame. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{5}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X>52).$ 

We know that $P(X<48)=0.25.$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<48) & =0.25 \\ P(Z<\frac{48-\mu }{5}) & =0.25 \\ Φ(\frac{48-\mu }{5}) & =0.25 \\ \frac{48-\mu }{5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.25)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.25)=-0.6745.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{48-\mu }{5} & =-0.6745 \\ 48-\mu  & =-3.3725 \\ \mu  & =51.3725.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(52<X)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>52) & =P(Z>\frac{52-51.3725}{5}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.13) \\  & =1-Φ(0.13) \\  & =1-0.5517 \\  & ≈44.83%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $44.83%$ of the frames take longer than $52$ minutes.
